extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, agency counsel, and administrative law practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements from the Administrative Procedure Act (House Report) governing federal agency rulemaking, adjudication, hearings, records, judicial review, examiners, and related duties. Usable as a checklist for agency actions and for evaluating agency compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency definition and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Agency" means each authority... of the Government of the United States other than Congress, the courts, or the governments of the possessions, Territories, or the District of Columbia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists explicit exclusions (e.g., agencies composed of representatives of parties to disputes, courts-martial, military or naval authority in the field in time of war, functions expiring on termination of present hostilities, and specified wartime statutes). Except as to section 3 requirements, those exclusions remove certain bodies from operation of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person and party definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Person" includes individuals, partnerships, corporations, associations, or public or private organizations... "Party" includes any person or agency named or admitted as a party, or properly seeking and entitled as of right to be admitted as a party, in any agency proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may admit others as parties for limited purposes; definitions determine who has rights (notice, participation, review) under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of rule and rule making
rubrics_metrics.description: "Rule" means the whole or any part of any agency statement of general or particular applicability and future effect designed to implement, interpret, or prescribe law or policy... "Rule making" means agency process for the formulation, amendment, or repeal of a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rule types (rates, wages, prices, valuations, accounting, practices) and distinguishes rules from rules addressed to named persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of order and adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: "Order" means the whole or any part of the final disposition... of any agency in any matter other than rule making but including licensing. "Adjudication" means agency process for the formulation of an order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies which agency actions are adjudications and thus subject to adjudication procedures in the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of license and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: "License" includes the whole or part of any agency permit, certificate, approval, registration, charter, membership, statutory exemption... "Licensing" includes agency process respecting the grant, renewal, denial, revocation, suspension... of a license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadly defines license-related actions subject to licensing procedures and protections in the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of sanction and relief
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sanction" includes prohibition, withholding of relief, imposition of penalty or fine, seizure of property, assessment of damages, revocation of license, or other compulsory action; "Relief" includes grants of money, license, recognition of claim, or other beneficial action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the forms of agency action that may impose burdens or confer benefits and hence are subject to Act protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public information — publication of organization, procedures, and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall separately state and currently publish in the Federal Register (1) descriptions of its central and field organization... (2) statements of the general course and method by which its functions are channeled and determined... and (3) substantive rules adopted as authorized by law and statements of general policy or interpretations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No person may be required to resort to organization or procedure not so published; publication requirement excludes functions requiring secrecy in the public interest or matters solely internal to agency management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public information — publication of opinions and orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall publish or, in accordance with published rule, make available to public inspection all final opinions or orders in the adjudication of cases (except those required for good cause to be held confidential and not cited as precedents) and all rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must make precedential/adjudicative dispositions available for public inspection unless confidentiality for good cause is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public records access
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters of official record shall in accordance with published rule be made available to persons properly and directly concerned except information held confidential for good cause found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory exceptions aside, agencies must provide access to official records for persons with proper interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: General notice of proposed rule making shall be published in the Federal Register... and shall include (1) a statement of the time, place, and nature of public rule-making proceedings; (2) reference to the authority under which the rule is proposed; and (3) either the terms or substance of the proposed rule or a description of the subjects and issues involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice exception applies where all persons subject are named and personally served or have actual notice; statutory exceptions and agency 'good cause' findings (impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to public interest) permit omission of notice; interpretative rules, policy statements, and rules of agency organization/procedure are exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking participation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: After notice required by this section, the agency shall afford interested persons an opportunity to participate in the rule making through submission of written data, views, or argument with or without opportunity to present the same orally in any manner; and, after consideration of all relevant matter presented, the agency shall incorporate in any rules adopted a concise general statement of their basis and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where statute requires rulemaking on the record after an agency hearing, sections 7 and 8 apply instead; agencies must consider all relevant submissions and state basis and purpose in rule promulgation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule effective date minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: The required publication or service of any substantive rule ... shall be made not less than thirty days prior to the effective date thereof except as otherwise provided by the agency upon good cause found and published with the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive rules generally require a 30-day delay before taking effect unless the agency publishes a good-cause justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to petition for rule issuance, amendment, or repeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall accord any interested person the right to petition for the issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms an affirmative right of interested persons to request rulemaking action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication — notice of hearing contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons entitled to notice of an agency hearing shall be timely informed of (1) the time, place, and nature thereof; (2) the legal authority and jurisdiction under which the hearing is to be held; and (3) the matters of fact and law asserted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When private persons are moving parties, other parties must promptly notify issues contested; agencies may by rule require responsive pleadings; times/places must regard convenience and necessity of parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication — participation and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall afford all interested parties opportunity for (1) the submission and consideration of facts, argument, offers of settlement, or proposals of adjustment... and (2) to the extent that the parties are unable so to determine any controversy by consent, hearing, and decision upon notice and in conformity with sections 7 and 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must permit submission of facts and arguments; when parties cannot resolve by consent, formal hearing and decision procedures apply as specified in later sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of functions / ex parte restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The same officers who preside at the reception of evidence pursuant to section 7 shall make the recommended decision or initial decision required by section 8... Save to the extent required for the disposition of ex parte matters as authorized by law, no such officer shall consult any person or party on any fact in issue unless upon notice and opportunity for all parties to participate; nor shall such officer be responsible to or subject to the supervision or direction of any officer, employee, or agent engaged in investigative or prosecuting functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits investigative/prosecutorial staff from advising or participating in adjudicative decisions in the same or factually related cases, except as witness or counsel; provides limited exceptions (initial licenses, public utilities, or body-comprising members).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory orders authorized
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency is authorized in its sound discretion, with like effect as in the case of other orders, to issue a declaratory order to terminate a controversy or remove uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may employ declaratory orders as a mechanism to resolve uncertainty analogous to other orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of appearance and counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person compelled to appear in person before any agency... shall be accorded the right to be accompanied, represented, and advised by counsel or, if permitted by the agency, by other qualified representative. Every party shall be accorded the right to appear in person or by or with counsel or other duly qualified representative in any agency proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals entitled to be represented; agencies should proceed with reasonable dispatch but respect convenience/necessity of parties; does not grant or deny non-lawyers the right to represent others unless provided by law or rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigations — authorization and access to transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: No process, requirement of a report, inspection, or other investigative act or demand shall be issued, made, or enforced in any manner or for any purpose except as authorized by law. Every person compelled to submit data or evidence shall be entitled to retain or, on payment of lawfully prescribed costs, procure a copy or transcript thereof, except that in a nonpublic investigatory proceeding the witness may for good cause be limited to inspection of the official transcript of his testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigatory powers must be grounded in law; witnesses have right to copies of evidence/transcripts subject to cost and limited confidentiality exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena issuance and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency subpoenas authorized by law shall be issued to any party upon request and, as may be required by rules of procedure, upon a statement or showing of general relevance and reasonable scope of the evidence sought. Upon contest the court shall sustain any such subpoena... to the extent that it is found to be in accordance with law, and... shall issue an order requiring appearance or production under penalty for contempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoenas should be issued on request with reasonable scope; judicial enforcement requires showing accordance with law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial notices — promptness and statement of grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt notice shall be given of the denial in whole or in part of any written application, petition, or other request... Except in affirming a prior denial or where the denial is self-explanatory, such notice shall be accompanied by a simple statement of procedural or other grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must promptly notify applicants of denials and provide procedural or other grounds unless self-explanatory or reaffirming prior denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearings — presiding officers and disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall preside at the taking of evidence (1) the agency, (2) one or more members of the body which comprises the agency, or (3) one or more examiners appointed as provided in this Act; The functions of all presiding officers... shall be conducted in an impartial manner. Any such officer may at any time withdraw if he deems himself disqualified; and, upon the filing in good faith of a timely and sufficient affidavit of personal bias or disqualification... the agency shall determine the matter as a part of the record and decision in the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officers must be impartial; formal mechanism for disqualification and agency determination on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing powers of presiding officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers presiding at hearings shall have authority... to (1) administer oaths and affirmations, (2) issue subpoenas authorized by law, (3) rule upon offers of proof and receive relevant evidence, (4) take or cause depositions..., (5) regulate the course of the hearing, (6) hold conferences for settlement or simplification, (7) dispose of procedural requests, (8) make or recommend decisions in conformity with section 8, and (9) take any other action authorized by agency rule consistent with this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates core procedural authorities necessary to manage hearings effectively and fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence rules and burden of proof at hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as statutes otherwise provide, the proponent of a rule or order shall have the burden of proof. Any oral or documentary evidence may be received, but every agency shall as a matter of policy provide for the exclusion of irrelevant, immaterial, or unduly repetitious evidence and no sanction shall be imposed or rule or order be issued except upon consideration of the whole record... and as supported by and in accordance with the reliable, probative, and substantial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties have rights to present, rebut, and cross-examine; agencies may adopt written-evidence procedures where interests not prejudiced (e.g., rulemaking, money/benefit claims, initial licenses). 'Whole record' and 'substantial evidence' standards apply where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record — exclusive record for decision and access
rubrics_metrics.description: The transcript of testimony and exhibits, together with all papers and requests filed in the proceeding, shall constitute the exclusive record for decision in accordance with section 8 and, upon payment of lawfully prescribed costs, shall be made available to the parties. Where any agency decision rests on official notice of a material fact not appearing in the evidence in the record, any party shall on timely request be afforded an opportunity to show the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The official transcript/exhibits/papers form the exclusive record; parties may obtain copies on payment and challenge official notice-based facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions — initial decision, certification, and appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases in which the agency has not presided at the reception of the evidence, the officer who presided... shall initially decide the case or the agency shall require... the entire record to be certified to it for initial decision. Whenever such officers make the initial decision and in the absence of either an appeal to the agency or review upon motion of the agency within time provided by rule, such decision shall... become the decision of the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies initial decision-making by presiding officers, certification of record, and conversion of initial decisions into agency decisions absent timely appeal or review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to submit proposed findings and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to each recommended, initial, or tentative decision... the parties shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity to submit... (1) proposed findings and conclusions, or (2) exceptions to the decisions or recommended decisions... and (3) supporting reasons for such exceptions or proposed findings or conclusions. The record shall show the ruling upon each such finding, conclusion, or exception presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must be given reasonable opportunity to submit proposed findings/exceptions and the record must reflect rulings on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision content — findings, reasons, and disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: All decisions... shall become a part of the record and include a statement of (1) findings and conclusions, as well as the reasons or basis therefor, upon all the material issues of fact, law, or discretion presented on the record; and (2) the appropriate rule, order, sanction, relief, or denial thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must explicitly state findings and legal/ factual bases and identify the agency disposition and any rules or sanctions applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on sanctions and rulemaking authority
rubrics_metrics.description: No sanction shall be imposed or substantive rule or order be issued except within jurisdiction delegated to the agency and as authorized by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may act only within delegated statutory authority; actions beyond delegation or not authorized by law are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing protections — notice, opportunity to comply, and renewal pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: In any case in which application is made for a license required by law the agency... shall set and complete any proceedings required to be conducted pursuant to sections 7 and 8... Except in cases of willfulness or those in which public health, interest, or safety requires otherwise, no withdrawal, suspension, revocation, or annulment of any license shall be lawful unless... facts or conduct which may warrant such action shall have been called to the attention of the licensee by the agency in writing and the licensee shall have been accorded opportunity to demonstrate or achieve compliance with all lawful requirements. In any case in which the licensee has... made timely and sufficient application for a renewal or a new license, no license... shall expire until such application shall have been finally determined by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects licensees by requiring written pre-notice of conduct warranting sanction and chance to comply; ensures renewal applications suspend expiration until final determination except limited public-health/willfulness exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to judicial review (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person suffering legal wrong because of any agency action, or adversely affected or aggrieved by such action... shall be entitled to judicial review thereof, except so far as (1) statutes preclude judicial review or (2) agency action is by law committed to agency discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms right of persons harmed by agency actions to seek judicial review unless expressly precluded or committed to agency discretion by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and venue of judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: The form of proceeding for judicial review shall be any special statutory review proceeding relevant to the subject matter in any court specified by statute or, in the absence or inadequacy thereof, any applicable form of legal action... in any court of competent jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits specialized statutory review procedures where provided; otherwise courts of competent jurisdiction may hear appropriate forms of action (declaratory judgments, injunctions, habeas corpus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewable acts and exhaustion principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency action made reviewable by statute and every final agency action for which there is no other adequate remedy in any court shall be subject to judicial review. Any preliminary, procedural, or intermediate agency action or ruling not directly reviewable shall be subject to review upon the review of the final agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final agency actions are generally reviewable; intermediate rulings are reviewable as part of final-action review; agencies can adopt rules requiring timely administrative appeals as prerequisite to judicial review (exhaustion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim relief and stay authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending judicial review any agency is authorized, where it finds that justice so requires, to postpone the effective date of any action taken by it. Upon such conditions... every reviewing court... is authorized to issue all necessary and appropriate process to postpone the effective date of any agency action or to preserve status or rights pending conclusion of the review proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both agencies and courts have authority to delay or preserve status pending judicial review when justice requires and to prevent irreparable injury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of judicial review and standards for setting aside agency action
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing court shall decide all relevant questions of law... It shall (A) compel agency action unlawfully withheld or unreasonably delayed; and (B) hold unlawful and set aside agency action, findings, and conclusions found to be (1) arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, or otherwise not in accordance with law; (2) contrary to constitutional right, power, privilege, or immunity; (3) in excess of statutory jurisdiction, authority, or limitations, or short of statutory right; (4) without observance of procedure required by law; (5) unsupported by substantial evidence in any case subject to the requirements of sections 7 and 8 or otherwise reviewed on the record of an agency hearing provided by statute; or (6) unwarranted by the facts to the extent that the facts are subject to trial de novo by the reviewing court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates the primary grounds and evidentiary standards for judicial invalidation or remand of agency actions; courts review whole record or portions cited by any party and consider prejudicial error rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners — appointment, duties, removal, and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be appointed by and for each agency as many qualified and competent examiners as may be necessary for proceedings pursuant to sections 7 and 8, who shall be assigned to cases in rotation so far as practicable and shall perform no duties inconsistent with their duties and responsibilities as examiners. Examiners shall be removable by the agency... only for good cause established and determined by the Civil Service Commission... after opportunity for hearing and upon the record thereof. Examiners shall receive compensation prescribed by the Commission independently of agency recommendations or ratings...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must be qualified, rotated, shielded from inconsistent duties, and removable only for good cause with Civil Service Commission process; compensation set independently to avoid agency influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil Service Commission powers regarding examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of this section, the Commission is authorized to make investigations, require reports by agencies, issue reports, including an annual report to the Congress, promulgate rules, appoint such advisory committees as may be deemed necessary, recommend legislation, subpena witnesses or records, and pay witness fees as established for the United States courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission has investigatory, rulemaking, and oversight authority to implement examiner protections and related functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction — preservation of constitutional rights and equal application of procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Act shall be held to diminish the constitutional rights of any person or to limit or repeal additional requirements imposed by statute or otherwise recognized by law. Except as otherwise required by law, all requirements or privileges relating to evidence or procedure shall apply equally to agencies and persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Act does not supplant constitutional protections or more stringent statutory requirements; procedural/evidentiary requirements generally apply equally to agencies and persons unless law provides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction — severability, agency authority to comply, and effective dates
rubrics_metrics.description: If any provision of this Act... is held invalid, the remainder... shall not be affected. Every agency is granted all authority necessary to comply with the requirements of this Act through the issuance of rules or otherwise. This Act shall take effect three months after its approval except that sections 7 and 8 shall take effect six months after such approval, the requirement of the selection of examiners pursuant to section 11 shall not become effective until one year after such approval, and no procedural requirement shall be mandatory as to any agency proceeding initiated prior to the effective date of such requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides severability, grants agencies power to adopt rules to implement Act requirements, and sets staggered effective dates for different procedural provisions.
